title: jurisdictional-proof-guard-and-retention-orchestration
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: Customers with regional data restrictions and strict retention SLAs cannot reliably map live telemetry to SOC 2 / ISO 27001 control artifacts. We need a single orchestration layer that: (1) maps runtime signals to the correct control assertions based on jurisdiction and service configuration, (2) enforces retention bounds and redaction rules at the evidence-collector level, and (3) assembles tamper-evident attestation bundles for audits.

Goal: Deliver a Policy-driven 'Proof Guard' and Retention Orchestrator that automatically classifies, collects, and bundles evidence per-jurisdiction and per-control, integrates with Redwood Private VPC collectors, and surfaces audit-ready artifacts to the Console and auditor exports. This reduces manual evidence stitching and accelerates SOC 2 / ISO attestation by automating provenance metadata and retention enforcement.
acceptance_criteria: Collectors can tag telemetry with jurisdiction and control_id at ingestion (50% of common event types) using the Proof Guard classifier
Retention Orchestrator enforces per-tenant retention policies with soft-delete and automated redaction for at least three storage backends (S3, GCS, local NFS)
Attestation bundles include provenance metadata (hash chain, collector id, timestamp, policy version) and can be exported as auditor-ready ZIPs from Console
Automated test suite covers control mapping rules and retention enforcement with CI that fails on policy drift
Docs and a Developer Quickstart are published: Confluence playbook + sample collector config + example export
tasks: Design: proof-guard rule language and default policy set
Engineering: collector SDK changes to emit control_id and provenance headers
Engineering: retention orchestrator service with policy engine and backend adapters
Console: export UI + auditor zip builder + verification view
QA: integration tests for retention enforcement, redaction, and bundle integrity
Security: threat modeling and review for export signing and key management
Docs: playbook and runbook for on-prem/private deployments
architecture_notes: High-level: introduce a lightweight Proof Guard classifier in the collector SDK that attaches normalized control_id tags (e.g., "control:CC6.1") and provenance headers (collector_id, local_seq, sha256 of payload). A Retention Orchestrator service subscribes to the collector stream (Kafka/backplane) and applies tenant policy rules (jurisdiction + control mapping + retention TTL). When an evidence export is requested or scheduled, the Orchestrator materializes an attestation bundle: compressed artifacts + signed manifest (HMAC or KMS-backed signature) + hash chain. Use pluggable storage adapters to support hosted buckets and on-prem NFS. Ensure rollout path for Redwood Private where collector -> Orchestrator communication can be proxied via customer VPC connectors.
risks: Policy complexity: mapping edge-cases between regional law and SOC 2 control phrasing may require legal review
Performance: additional metadata emission and retention checks could increase ingest latency under peak load
Storage costs: automated snapshots for auditability increase retained volume unless deduplication is applied
Backward compatibility: existing collectors without classifier will need a fallback mapping strategy
rollout_plan: 1) Feature-flag the collector SDK changes and deploy to a pilot tenant; 2) Enable Retention Orchestrator in read-only mode (dry-run) to validate mappings for 2 weeks; 3) Iterate on rule set and ergonomics with Compliance team and one customer pilot; 4) Flip enforcement and enable export signing; 5) Publish runbook and open availability to paid tiers. Each step includes a health-check dashboard and rollback plan.
